findings.claim: The new gate fails open on dangling references whose component key is an Object.prototype property name: hasTarget uses `components[section][key] !== undefined` on prototype-ful objects returned by js-yaml, so `#/components/<any-section>/constructor` (also toString, __proto__, valueOf, hasOwnProperty, ...) resolves against the JS prototype chain instead of the document, in all ten component sections and in both discriminator.mapping forms. This falsifies the receipt's enforcementPlacement claim that 'a misrouted path can never report green' / the code comment's totality-by-construction claim, and it is the same defect class the lane exists to close (resolution decided by something other than document content — prototype chain instead of truncated prefix). It is also strictly weaker than the OLD Rust control on the one input class both layers see: compose's BTreeSet lookup would report a block-style `$ref: '#/components/schemas/constructor'` as DanglingRef, the new gate stays silent.
findings.failureScenario: An author (or a compose fail-open) publishes `$ref: '#/components/schemas/constructor'` or `discriminator.mapping: {x: constructor}` with no such schema defined. The real document is above both floors, findings stay 0, the gate prints green, and the dangling ref ships to every generated client. Proven: fixture at /tmp/critic-ann-probes/protochain/backend/openapi/openapi.yaml (schemas Todo+Wrapper+Union; Wrapper properties a/b/c $ref '#/components/schemas/constructor', '.../toString', '.../__proto__'; Union discriminator mapping `ghost: constructor`); `node scripts/check-openapi-refs.mjs /tmp/critic-ann-probes/protochain` reports 'FAILED: 0 finding(s), 3 refs, 1 mapping entries' — zero findings for three dangling refs and one ghost mapping name; only the floor failed the tiny fixture. Differential control: the same run shape reports `Missing` as dangling (merge-key probe: 'dangling reference `#/components/schemas/Missing`'), so the silence is key-specific, not fixture setup.
